land.text: the German-Austrian lands of the Dual Monarchy

predecessors.note: The Anschluss page: after the Austro-Hungarian Empire fell in 1918 'the new Republic of German-Austria attempted to form a union with Germany'. The Republic of German-Austria claimed more than it kept (South Tyrol, Sudeten lands).

land.text: the whole state, the province of 'Ostmark'

successors.note: 'Austria became the province of Ostmark, and Seyss-Inquart was appointed governor.' The Second Republic (1945) is a separate dossier whose predecessor is Nazi Germany.

correction.text: the 1919 shape without South Tyrol, borrowed for 1918

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row starts in 1919 but the Republic of German-Austria followed the Dual Monarchy's fall in 1918. The corrected 1919 shape (below) is borrowed; unverified for 1918 beyond the year. No area figure is given by the pages opened, so the infobox comparison cannot be made.

87,213 km2 (no area on the pages to compare). The shape holds South Tyrol (20 cells, about 5,000 km2) and only 2 of Burgenland's 14 cells; the Treaty of Saint-Germain (signed 10 September 1919) gave 'German-populated South Tyrol to Italy' and 'a portion of the Alpine provinces' to the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes. The year-end state is without South Tyrol; Burgenland came in 1921.

85,624 km2 (-1,589 km2 on 1919): South Tyrol is out; three border cells of Italy remain, which are within the shape's precision. The shape already holds all of Burgenland, a year early: 'Through the Treaty of St. Germain it became part of the Austrian Republic in 1921', and 'the provincial capital city of Sopron remained in Hungary'. The Carinthian plebiscite of 10 October 1920 left south-eastern Carinthia with Austria. No area on the pages to compare.

85,328 km2 (-296 km2 on 1935), unexplained by the pages opened; the Republic of Austria became the Federal State of Austria on 1 May 1934 (a regime change; the state, its territory and its capital continue).

correction.text: the 1936 shape, annexed by Germany on 12-13 March 1938

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row ends in 1937 but the Anschluss was on 12-13 March 1938 ('On the morning of 12 March 1938, the 8th Army of the German Wehrmacht crossed the border into Austria'). The 1936 shape holds for the first months of 1938.

region.text: German-Austria, the German-speaking lands of the Dual Monarchy

ledger.note: 1918: the Republic of German-Austria arises from the Dual Monarchy. 'the new Republic of German-Austria attempted to form a union with Germany after the Austro-Hungarian Empire fell in 1918'; the Treaties of Saint-Germain and Versailles 'forbade both the union and the continued use of the name'. The page gives the year only.

region.text: south-eastern Carinthia, inhabited partly by Slovenians, the plebiscite area

ledger.note: 1919: the dispute over south-eastern Carinthia. The page says the south-east 'was inhabited partly by Slovenians' and gives only the plebiscite of 1920; the start of the dispute is a bridge over a silence.

10 September 1919: the Treaty of Saint-Germain gives South Tyrol to Italy. The republic 'was created after the signing of the Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye on 10 September 1919', which ceded 'German-populated South Tyrol to Italy'; German-Austria changed its name to the Republic of Austria. The shape drops South Tyrol in 1920.

region.text: a portion of the Alpine provinces (Lower Styria around Maribor is the researcher's reading; the page does not name it)

ledger.note: 10 September 1919: a part of the Alpine provinces goes to the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes. The page says 'a portion of the Alpine provinces' and does not name Lower Styria; the land was never in Cliopatria's Austrian shape.

region.text: south-eastern Carinthia, inhabited partly by Slovenians, the plebiscite area

ledger.note: 10 October 1920: the Carinthian plebiscite keeps the south-east in Austria. 'a Carinthian plebiscite on October 10, 1920, and the majority chose to remain with Austria'.

region.text: Burgenland (West Hungary, 'part of the Hungarian kingdom since 907')

ledger.note: 1921: Burgenland joins Austria. 'Through the Treaty of St. Germain it became part of the Austrian Republic in 1921'; the provincial capital Sopron 'remained in Hungary' (this page does not date the plebiscite; the Hungarian dossier gives December 1921). Cliopatria's 1920 shape already holds Burgenland.

1 May 1934: the Republic of Austria becomes the Federal State of Austria. 'On 1 May 1934, Dollfuss created a one-party state. The name of the country was changed from the Republic of Austria to the Federal State of Austria.' (Dollfuss took power on 20 May 1932 and suspended parliament in March 1933.)

12-13 March 1938: Germany annexes Austria (the Anschluss). 'On the morning of 12 March 1938, the 8th Army of the German Wehrmacht crossed the border into Austria'; 'The Anschluss was given immediate effect by legislative act on 13 March', ratified by the referendum of 10 April 1938 (99.7%). Schuschnigg resigned on 11 March.

12 March 1938: the Republic of Austria ceases to exist. 'With the Anschluss, the Republic of Austria ceased to exist as an independent state'; 'Austria became the province of Ostmark'. Annulled in 1943 (Moscow Declaration) and on 27 April 1945.

wars.name: Carinthian plebiscite dispute

zones.text: south-eastern Carinthia, inhabited partly by Slovenians, the plebiscite area

wars.outcome: Plebiscite of 10 October 1920: 'the majority chose to remain with Austria'; no land changed hands.
wars.note: The fighting of 1919 is not on the page; the zone is the plebiscite area.

certainty.note: The republic claimed more than it kept until Saint-Germain was signed on 10 September 1919; South Tyrol was Italian-occupied.
Saint-Germain, the Carinthian plebiscite (10 October 1920) and Burgenland (1921) fixed the lines.

notes: Cliopatria 'Republic of Austria' (1919-1937, Q40) is the First Republic and its Federal State of Austria (1934-1938); the Wikidata id Q40 is shared with no other row but the Second Republic is a separate row ('Second Republic of Austria', 1946-2024) with its own dossier. The Anschluss is dated 12-13 March 1938, so a 1938 keyframe is added. Cliopatria shape checks (gazetteer cells, not pages): the 1919 shape holds South Tyrol (20 cells) and 2 of 14 Burgenland cells; the 1920 shape holds all of Burgenland and 2 South Tyrol cells; three cells of Italy and three of Germany stay in every shape (border noise). Not on the pages opened: the date of the Republic of German-Austria (12 November 1918), the treaty's entry into force (16 July 1920), the Sopron plebiscite date (see the Hungarian dossier), the Sudeten and Lower Styria cessions' boundaries (the Sudeten lands and Lower Styria were not held by Austria in any shape; no events written for Czechoslovakia), the rulers, any area figure, and the Carinthian fighting of 1919. Two pages only (budget 1-2).
